subject: Coding a factor as a covariate for QTL analysis

messages.author: 13d6aa0007c15012
messages.subject: Coding a factor as a covariate for QTL analysis
parts:
For the data set I am working on, we decided we would like to include the grandmother and F1 mother as covariates. I am concerned that I have not coded these correctly into their numeric form, as when I added these two covariates, the computation time increased significantly.

There are four grandmothers and ten F1 females. This is approach I have taken:

>grandparent <- as.numeric(pull.pheno(sawfly.cross, pheno.col=20)) 

>fromg1 <- as.numeric(grandparent == 1)

>fromg2 <- as.numeric(grandparent == 2)

>fromg3 <- as.numeric(grandparent == 3)

>fromg4 <- as.numeric(grandparent == 4)

>grandparentx <- cbind(fromg1, fromg2, fromg3, fromg4)


I used similar coding to pull out the information for the F1 mothers. I then pulled all the covariates together using this code:


>allcovar <- cbind(head.covar, grandparentx, motherx)


Is this the right away to approach this? I will note that in the phenotype column, the grandparents or mothers are coded simply as 1-4 or 1-10.
